items.name: Lead magnet: promote the Template Pack, don't replace the Playbook
items.what: Build a new primary magnet — a 'Fulfillment Update Template Pack' (5-8 paste-ready templates: delay announcement, backer apology, status-page copy, refund-request response, proof-of-life update, milestone-slip notice) — seeded from the founder's real COVID-era comms and the existing WISMO teardown template. Keep the Presale Anxiety Playbook live as a secondary/companion asset, not a replacement. Feature the Template Pack as the CTA on organic content (X/Reddit/LinkedIn posts, WISMO teardowns); offer the Playbook inside the nurture sequence as the 'why this works' companion piece.
items.how: Reuse the existing landing-page/capture pattern already built for the Playbook — same form, same list, new asset behind it. No new page architecture, no new tool. Draft the templates from the founder's own fulfillment-crisis comms (proof-only: real language he actually used, not fabricated examples) plus the WISMO teardown's 'what a good update looks like' section. Ship as a single PDF/Notion doc, not an interactive tool (out of budget/time for a solo founder in 2 hrs/day).
items.evidence: Converging (if noisy) industry signal: templates/checklists consistently outconvert generic ebooks — ebooks cluster at 3-5% opt-in with only ~12% actually read; templates/checklists cluster at 8-25% with much higher consumption because the payoff is immediate and the buyer can use it in under 3 minutes. A named practitioner account on Indie Hackers describes a checklist assembled in ~15 minutes pulling 200 leads, and a separate SaaS-founder account reports ~100 signups off a template magnet with ~5% converting to paying customers. Caveat: most of the specific percentage stats in this space (digitalapplied.com, amraandelma.com, subpage.co, prospeo.io, zeliq.com) read as AI-generated SEO listicle content with suspiciously precise, uncited numbers — treat the exact percentages as directional folklore, not proof. The consistent qualitative finding across every source (folklore and practitioner alike) — narrow + immediately usable beats broad + educational for opt-in rate — is the load-bearing part, not any single number.

items.name: Capture: don't rebuild, extend
items.what: The existing Playbook capture form/page is the single point of entry for both magnets. One form, one list, one welcome flow — the Template Pack is just a second file behind the same gate (or a second CTA on the same page offering 'the playbook' vs 'the templates').
items.how: Add a second delivery block to the existing capture automation (same email-address field, same consent checkbox/CASL language) rather than standing up a new landing page or a new form tool.
items.evidence: No new evidence needed beyond the brief's constraint that the Playbook capture already works — this is a build-around-what-exists call, not a research finding.

items.name: Nurture: short, urgent, 4-6 emails, then a low-frequency trickle — not a 12-month drip
items.what: Email 1 (Day 0, instant): deliver the magnet + one-sentence 'here's what to do with it today.' Email 2 (Day 2): the specific pain — what happens when backer comms go silent (ties to WISMO teardown). Email 3 (Day 5): proof — the founder's own COVID fulfillment story, plain language, no fabricated metrics. Email 4 (Day 8): objection handler — 'this isn't a chatbot, it's a way to never promise a hard date and still look calm.' Email 5 (Day 11): the ask — private-offer CTA for the free pilot, low-commitment framing ('no card, no contract, I'll set it up with you personally'). Email 6 (Day 14, only for non-clickers): last short nudge, then drop to a monthly 'still drowning?' check-in for the remainder of the 3-4 month consideration window instead of continuing to drip weekly.
items.how: Behavior-based branching: a click on the pilot CTA at any point jumps the contact straight to a 'book a call' state and exits the sequence; no click by Day 14 downgrades to monthly cadence. Keep each email under ~300 words, one CTA each, follow roughly an 80/20 value-to-ask ratio across the sequence.
items.evidence: Standard 5-email nurture skeleton (hook → insight → proof → objection-handler → soft ask) and the every-3-7-day cadence, tightening on intent signals and slowing to biweekly/monthly on silence, is repeated consistently across nurture-sequence guides. The 'flow not stock' framing (this buyer's urgency has an end date — the campaign fulfills — so the sequence must resolve fast, not run for a year) is the brief's own logic applied to that standard skeleton, not a separate citation.

items.name: Email tool: use Resend, don't add a new vendor
items.what: Resend (already paid, already the trusted infra for tideover.app) now supports what this funnel needs: Audiences + Broadcasts for the sends, and Automations (shipped April 2026) for the timed/triggered sequence — event-driven with time-delay steps and branching, triggered via API/webhook. Free tier: 1,000 contacts, 3,000 emails/month, 100/day cap, one sending domain — enough headroom for a niche list that will stay small for a long time, at $0 marginal cost.
items.how: Wire the existing capture form to fire a `lead_magnet_downloaded` event to Resend on submit (one webhook call — trivial for a founder who already built the app's ingest/auth layers). Build the 6-email sequence as a Resend Automation on a dedicated Audience. Do this on a sending subdomain separate from both the product's transactional email (order-status, replies) and any cold-outreach domain — protects deliverability on all three lanes.
items.evidence: MailerLite's free tier was cut to 250 subscribers / 2,500 emails/month effective July 2026 (from 500/12,000) and caps free accounts at 3 automations — usable but thin and shrinking. Beehiiv's free Launch plan allows 2,500 active subscribers with unlimited sends but is a newsletter/publishing platform, not built for triggered lifecycle sequences, and would be a third vendor/domain to manage. Buttondown is free only to 100 subscribers and gates automation behind a separate $29/month add-on, which defeats the point of 'free' for a sequence-dependent funnel. Resend Automations is event/API-triggered rather than a drag-and-drop visual builder, which fits a technical solo founder and avoids tool sprawl entirely.

items.name: Two lists, two sending domains — never mixed
items.what: List A (Clean/express consent): people who opted in via the lead-magnet form. CASL express consent — documented, timestamped, opt-in checkbox. Sent from a dedicated marketing subdomain on Resend, separate from the app's transactional sending domain. List B (cold/implied consent): prospects found via outbound research per the existing campaign plan (LinkedIn/Reddit/X), contacted under CASL's implied-consent lane (public business email relevant to their role, or a recent inquiry within its 6-month window). This runs on a separate outreach tool and a separate purchased sending domain with its own warmup — never Resend's marketing subdomain, never the app's transactional domain. A reply or click on a cold email must never auto-add someone to List A; that would misrepresent the consent basis on record.
items.how: Enforce at the infrastructure level: separate Resend Audience + separate sending subdomain for List A; separate tool/domain for List B. Document consent method and timestamp per contact on List A (CASL requirement). Every commercial email on both lists carries a functional unsubscribe honored within CASL's mandated window.
items.evidence: CASL requires express consent (a clear opt-in action) before sending commercial electronic messages on the opt-in lane; consent is not time-limited once given. The implied-consent lane covers an existing business relationship (2-year window from last transaction), a recent inquiry/application (6-month window), or conspicuous publication of a business-relevant email address without a no-solicitation notice. CASL mandates sender identity, physical address, a working contact mechanism, and an unsubscribe mechanism honored within 10 business days; separately, Gmail/Yahoo's bulk-sender rules require RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe headers for bulk senders, and unsubscribes must stop mail within 48 hours under those platform rules. Resend handles the one-click unsubscribe headers and per-contact suppression automatically for Audiences/Broadcasts.

items.name: Conversion math — conservative, small-list sanity check
items.what: Rough funnel model for planning, not a forecast: dedicated landing page visit → magnet opt-in, conservative low end 5-10% (template pack, tightly targeted page) vs 3-5% for a generic ebook alone. Opt-in list → engages with nurture (opens/clicks at least once): no hard citation found for a niche founder-voice list this small; treat 30-50% as a reasoned assumption, not a cited stat — flag it as such when planning, don't build a revenue model on it. Nurture → takes the pilot CTA (books a call/replies): general SaaS visitor-to-trial benchmarks run 2.1-7.1%, but that's for cold/generic traffic; a warm, opted-in list whose buyer is in acute, present-tense pain plausibly clears the high end of that range or beats it — again an estimate, not a citation. At the list sizes implied by this funnel (low hundreds), expect single-digit numbers of pilot conversations per month, not dozens — plan effort accordingly and don't over-build automation for volume that isn't there yet.
items.how: Track three numbers monthly: opt-in rate off the landing page, nurture engagement rate, CTA-click rate. Recompute the estimate after the first 20-30 opt-ins rather than trusting the ranges above past that point — the sample is small enough that real data beats any benchmark within the first month.
items.evidence: Visitor-to-lead benchmarks for B2B SaaS: 1.5-2.5% average, top 10% reach 8-15%; content-led organic pages typically 0.5-2.0%. Lead/visitor-to-trial: 2.1-7.1%. Template/checklist opt-in ranges of 8-25% appear repeatedly across sources but with weak/uncited methodology (see caveat in item 1) — used here only as a directional ceiling, not a promise.

items.name: Handoff to trial/pilot: private offer, not self-serve signup
items.what: The nurture sequence's terminal CTA is not a self-serve trial signup — it's a private, personally-offered free pilot ('reply to this email and I'll set you up myself'). This matches the buyer (a single overwhelmed founder, not a committee) and avoids building trial-signup infrastructure that doesn't exist yet.
items.how: CTA in email 5/6 is a reply-to-book or a Calendly-style link straight to the founder, not a product signup flow. Once booked, the pilot conversation is manual/high-touch — consistent with the founder's own 2 hrs/day GTM capacity and the tiny list size meaning single-digit conversations per month, not a funnel needing automated trial provisioning yet.
items.evidence: Consistent with the brief's own framing of the pilot as 'a private offer' and with the founder's stated bandwidth constraint (2 hrs/day, mostly already allocated) — a low-volume, high-touch handoff is the only one that fits the resourcing, independent of any external benchmark.

load_bearing_claims.claim: MailerLite's free plan was cut to 250 subscribers and 2,500 emails/month effective July 2026 (from 500 subscribers/12,000 emails), capped at 3 automations, 3 forms, 1 landing page.
Beehiiv's free Launch plan allows up to 2,500 active subscribers with unlimited sends.
Buttondown is free only to the first 100 subscribers; automation is a separate $29/month add-on, not included free.

Resend's free plan includes 1,000 contacts for Audiences/marketing, 3,000 emails/month (100/day cap), one sending domain; Resend Automations (event/API-triggered, with time-delay and branching steps) shipped April 2026.

CASL requires express (opt-in) consent before commercial email on the clean list; implied consent (covering the cold-outreach lane) applies for an existing business relationship for 2 years, a recent inquiry for 6 months, or conspicuously published business-relevant contact info; unsubscribe requests must be honored within 10 business days.

Templates/checklists outconvert generic long-form ebooks on both opt-in rate and consumption, though most published percentage figures in this space are low-confidence SEO-listicle content rather than verifiable primary data — the qualitative direction is corroborated by at least two independent practitioner accounts (Indie Hackers checklist-to-200-leads account; a SaaS founder's ~100-signup template-magnet account).

summary: Recommendation: build one new asset (a paste-ready Fulfillment Update Template Pack, seeded from the founder's real COVID comms + the existing WISMO teardown) as the featured magnet, keep the Playbook alive as a companion piece, and pipe both through the capture form that already works — no new page, no new tool for capture. Run a 4-6 email, ~14-day urgent nurture (not a long drip, because the buyer's pain has an end date) that branches on CTA clicks and downgrades non-responders to a monthly check-in for the rest of the 3-4 month window. Send it through Resend — already paid, already trusted — using its new Automations feature (event/API-triggered, shipped April 2026) and free-tier Audiences/Broadcasts (1,000 contacts, 3,000 emails/mo, $0 marginal cost); MailerLite's free tier just got cut to 250 subscribers, Buttondown gates automation behind a $29/mo add-on, and Beehiiv is a publishing platform that would add a third vendor/domain for no real gain. Enforce two fully separate lists and sending domains: the opt-in nurture list (CASL express consent, documented per-contact) on a Resend marketing subdomain, and any cold-outreach list (CASL implied consent) on a separate tool and domain — never let a cold reply auto-join the opt-in list. Conversion math is presented as conservative, labeled ranges (cited where possible, flagged as reasoned estimates where not) — expect single-digit pilot conversations per month at this list size, which matches the founder's actual bandwidth. The weakest part of the public evidence base is the specific lead-magnet conversion percentages: most "2026 statistics" sources read as AI-generated SEO content without verifiable methodology, so those numbers are used only directionally, not as promises.</summary>
